univariate_analysis.key_observation: Right-skew driven by long-tenure enterprise users; median is the more representative central measure for churn modelling.
univariate_analysis.recommended_viz: histogram with log-x or violin plot, split by plan_tier

univariate_analysis.key_observation: organic (38.4%) and paid_search (27.1%) dominate; 'unknown_legacy' is the 5th-largest bucket — non-trivial.
univariate_analysis.recommended_viz: bar chart, percentage labels, ordered descending

univariate_analysis.key_observation: 65% active / 22% voluntary / 13% involuntary — matches Phase 3's expected distribution.
Median user generates 12 events in their first 30 days; top 1% generate >500. Use median in Phase 5 group comparisons.
univariate_analysis.recommended_viz: log-scale histogram or box plot capped at p99

bivariate_analysis.key_finding: paid_search users churn voluntarily at 31% vs organic at 14% — more than 2× difference; involuntary churn rate is similar across channels (~12–14%).
bivariate_analysis.recommended_viz: stacked bar chart with annotated voluntary churn rate per channel
bivariate_analysis.reasoning: χ² statistic is large and the effect is concentrated in voluntary (not involuntary) churn, suggesting a product-fit or expectations-mismatch problem rather than payment friction. This is the single strongest segment-level signal in the data.

bivariate_analysis.key_finding: Users who churn voluntarily have a median of 6 events in their first 30 days vs 17 for retained users — a 65% gap.
bivariate_analysis.statistic: Mann-Whitney U = 8.2e9, p < 0.001; Cliff's δ = -0.42 (large effect)
bivariate_analysis.recommended_viz: grouped box plot, log-y, faceted by acquisition_channel
bivariate_analysis.reasoning: Both the median gap and Cliff's δ indicate this is a large effect, not just a statistically significant one. Effect size matters here because event-count is heavily right-skewed.

bivariate_analysis.key_finding: Voluntary churners have median tenure 91 days vs 412 for retained users; involuntary churn skews even earlier (median 47 days).
bivariate_analysis.recommended_viz: violin plot by churn_type, capped at p95
bivariate_analysis.reasoning: Confirms the classic 'churn happens early' pattern but the 47-day involuntary cluster suggests a separate payment-failure signal worth investigating in Phase 6.

bivariate_analysis.key_finding: Weekly churn count is ~480/week before 2025-07-15 and ~720/week in the four weeks after — a ~50% jump that does not appear in seasonal trends from 2024.
bivariate_analysis.statistic: Pre/post mean delta = +240/week (Welch's t, p < 0.001 against the pre-period)
bivariate_analysis.recommended_viz: line chart, marker at 2025-07-15, 7-day rolling average overlay
bivariate_analysis.reasoning: The discontinuity aligns with the pricing change (SQ3). Phase 5 should formally test this with an interrupted-time-series design rather than a simple t-test.

multivariate_patterns.pattern_observed: The negative event_count_30d ↔ voluntary churn relationship is sharpest for paid_search users (Cliff's δ = -0.55) and weakest for referral users (Cliff's δ = -0.18).
multivariate_patterns.business_interpretation: Paid_search users who never engage churn fast; referral users seem to give the product more benefit of the doubt regardless of engagement.
multivariate_patterns.recommended_followup: Phase 6 should investigate whether onboarding interventions targeted at low-engagement paid_search users could close the gap.

multivariate_patterns.pattern_observed: Starter-tier voluntary churn concentrates at days 28–35 (a 'first-bill' cliff); Pro tier shows no such cluster.
multivariate_patterns.business_interpretation: Starter users likely re-evaluate after their first credit-card statement; Pro users have already committed budget.
multivariate_patterns.recommended_followup: Phase 6 root cause: is this a pricing-perception issue or an unmet-value issue at day-28?

anomaly_catalogue.anomaly_description: A single acquisition_channel value 'partner' has 4× the involuntary-churn rate of every other channel (47% vs 11–14%).
possible_explanations: Partner channel sends users with weaker payment instruments (e.g., regional prepaid cards).
A specific partner relationship was sunset in 2025-Q2 and existing users were not migrated, causing failed renewals.

anomaly_catalogue.anomaly_description: Users with tenure_days < 7 and event_count_30d = 0 are 1.8% of the base but account for 9% of voluntary churn.
possible_explanations: Signups that never activated (likely test accounts or onboarding failures).
Misclassified involuntary churn that did not get a cancel_reason tag.

hypotheses.statement: There is a statistically significant difference in voluntary 90-day churn rate between paid_search and organic acquisition channels, with paid_search higher, in the Q3 cohort.
hypotheses.expected_test_type: Two-proportion z-test (or χ² with effect size)
hypotheses.reasoning: Bivariate analysis showed a large χ² effect concentrated in voluntary churn; this is the lead segment-level driver Phase 6 will need to trace to a root cause.

hypotheses.statement: There is a statistically significant negative association between event_count_30d and 90-day voluntary churn among users acquired in Q2 2025.
hypotheses.expected_test_type: Logistic regression with log(event_count) as predictor; Mann-Whitney U as the non-parametric confirmation
hypotheses.reasoning: Cliff's δ of -0.42 indicates a large effect; logistic regression will let Phase 5 estimate a per-event odds ratio for downstream intervention sizing.

hypotheses.statement: There is a statistically significant increase in weekly voluntary churn rate after 2025-07-15 vs the matching pre-period in the same Q3 cohort.
hypotheses.reasoning: Pre/post means differ but seasonal confounders cannot be ruled out by a naive t-test; segmented regression with a seasonal control isolates the pricing-change effect.

hypotheses.statement: There is a statistically significant interaction between acquisition_channel and event_count_30d in predicting voluntary churn (the engagement→retention slope is steeper for paid_search than for referral).
hypotheses.expected_test_type: Logistic regression with channel × log(events) interaction term
hypotheses.reasoning: Multivariate analysis revealed channel-dependent slope differences (δ = -0.55 vs -0.18). Testing the interaction formally tells Phase 6 whether onboarding intervention should be channel-targeted.

eda_visualisation_spec.insight_in_one_sentence: Paid-search voluntary churn (31%) is more than double organic (14%) — channel mix is a primary lever.
eda_visualisation_spec.reasoning: Stacked-bar keeps the within-channel proportions readable; using counts here would let channel size dominate the visual.

eda_visualisation_spec.insight_in_one_sentence: Voluntary churners engage at a fraction of retained users — and the gap widens for paid_search.
eda_visualisation_spec.reasoning: Log-y handles the power-law tail; facet by channel exposes the H4 interaction visually.

eda_visualisation_spec.insight_in_one_sentence: Weekly voluntary churn jumped ~50% after the 2025-07-15 pricing change.
eda_visualisation_spec.reasoning: Time-series view + a vertical marker at the change date communicates the discontinuity at a glance.

eda_visualisation_spec.chart_type: Density plot of tenure_days by plan_tier, faceted by churn_type
eda_visualisation_spec.insight_in_one_sentence: Starter-tier churners cluster at days 28–35 (the first-bill window).
eda_visualisation_spec.reasoning: Density plot exposes the modal cluster cleanly; a histogram would be sensitive to bin choice for this narrow window.

eda_visualisation_spec.insight_in_one_sentence: Event activity follows a long-tail power law — median (12) is more meaningful than mean (47).
eda_visualisation_spec.reasoning: Establishes for the Phase 7 audience why we report medians and use non-parametric tests.

phase_5_handoff.priority_order: H3 (pricing change is time-sensitive) → H1 (largest segment-level effect) → H2 (behavioural lever) → H4 (interaction; only meaningful if H1 and H2 both supported)
phase_5_handoff.notes: Multiple-testing correction will apply (4 hypotheses). Phase 5 should use Holm–Bonferroni at α=0.05. H3 requires a seasonal control series; the 2024 Q3 weekly churn series is the recommended baseline.
